mainTopic: How long a raised or dug-out area at a מבוי's entrance must be, according to רב יוסף and אביי, and the proofs each side brings.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an argument between רב יוסף and אביי. A מבוי whose קורה is too high can be fixed by raising the floor under it, and they argue how far that raised floor must reach: one טפח (רב יוסף) or four טפחים (אביי). The גמרא rejects the idea that they argue about using the space under the קורה. It then gives three other explanations: whether a קורה works as a היכר or as a מחיצה, whether a marker on the ground counts like a marker overhead, and whether there is a גזירה in case the raised floor wears down. Next comes a new case: a קורה lower than ten טפחים, where the ground beneath it is dug out. Here רב יוסף says the dug area must extend four טפחים and אביי says four אמות. The גמרא suggests their argument depends on רבי אמי ורבי אסי's ruling about a breached מבוי, but rejects this, because keeping an existing מבוי valid is different from creating a new one. אביי then brings two proofs that a מבוי needs four אמות, one from a ברייתא about courtyards and one from רב הונא's ruling about a protruding לחי, and רב יוסף answers both. Finally, with the word גופא, the גמרא begins to study רב הונא's ruling on its own, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The opinion requiring four טפחים forbids using the space under the beam
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its first suggested explanation. The one who requires four טפחים (אביי) holds that it is forbidden to use the area under the קורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who said four טפחים holds that it is forbidden to use the area under the cross beam!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its first proposal for why רב יוסף and אביי disagree. The one-טפח side lets you use the area under the beam, but the four-טפחים side does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the space under the קורה is not part of the usable alley, the raised floor cannot rely on that space. So a real, usable raised area of four טפחים is needed inside the alley itself. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא will reject this whole explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said (refers to the holder of an opinion)
He holds / he is of the opinion
To make use of the area directly beneath the cross beam
Four (here: four טפחים)

phrases.english: And the one who said four (handbreadths)
phrases.notes: This is אביי, according to the earlier part of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: holds: it is forbidden to use the area beneath the cross beam!
phrases.notes: This finishes the suggested explanation. The first half, about the one-טפח view, was on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proposed explanation that began on the previous amud, which tied the one-טפח view to permitting use beneath the קורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under this suggestion, the four-טפחים view holds that the area under the קורה may not be used, so a full four-טפחים raised area is required.

steps.title: Rejected: everyone permits using the space under the beam; the real question is marker versus wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says no: both sides agree that one may use the area under the קורה. Their real argument is whether a קורה works as a היכר (marker) or as a מחיצה (wall).
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that it is permitted to use the area under the beam. Here is what they argue about: one Master holds the beam serves as a marker, and the other holds the beam serves as a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first explanation and replaces it with a new one. The argument is about what a קורה actually does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the קורה is just a היכר (a visible sign separating the alley from רשות הרבים), even one טפח of raised floor is noticeable enough. That is רב יוסף's view. If the קורה acts as a מחיצה (we imagine its edge coming down as a wall), a wall needs at least four טפחים to count, so the raised area must be four טפחים. That is אביי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (both sides agree)
They disagree
Master (refers to one side of the dispute)
A noticeable marker or sign
A partition or wall

steps.confusionAlert: The two "מָר" do not name anyone directly. The first is רב יוסף (one טפח, היכר) and the second is אביי (four טפחים, מחיצה).
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether a קורה works as a היכר or as a מחיצה is a basic issue in the laws of מבוי, and it comes up again and again in עירובין.

phrases.english: No, for everyone holds
phrases.notes: "לָא" signals that the previous explanation is being rejected.

phrases.english: it is permitted to use the area beneath the cross beam,
and in this they disagree:
one Master holds a beam works as a marker,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף: one טפח is enough, since even that is noticeable.

phrases.english: and one Master holds a beam works as a partition.
phrases.notes: אביי: a wall needs at least four טפחים.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא קָסָבְרִי מוּתָּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ תַּחַת הַקּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation in step 1 and offers a new reason for the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the dispute is about using the area under the קורה. The dispute between רב יוסף and אביי itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sides actually agree that using the area under the beam is permitted, so that cannot be what they argue about. The real issue is how the קורה works: as a היכר or as a מחיצה.

steps.title: Second explanation: does a marker on the ground count like a marker overhead?
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both agree that a קורה is a היכר. They argue whether a marker below (the raised floor) is treated like a marker above (the beam).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: everyone agrees the beam is a marker. Here they argue about a marker below and a marker above. One Master holds we say a marker below is like a marker above; the other holds we do not say a marker below is like a marker above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to explain the dispute. This time both sides agree that the קורה is just a marker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The raised floor is a "marker below" and the beam is a "marker above." רב יוסף says the ground marker works just like the beam, so one טפח is enough, just as a beam of one טפח width is enough. אביי says a marker on the ground is less noticeable than one overhead, so it must be bigger: four טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative explanation)
A marker below (the raised floor)
A marker above (the cross beam)
We say / we apply the principle

phrases.english: And if you wish, say,
that everyone agrees a beam works as a marker,
and here, about a marker below
and a marker above they disagree,
for one Master holds we say

phrases.aramaic: הֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַטָּה כְּהֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַעְלָה,
phrases.english: a marker below is like a marker above,
and one Master holds we do not say

phrases.aramaic: הֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַטָּה כְּהֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַעְלָה.
phrases.english: a marker below is like a marker above.
phrases.notes: So the ground marker must be four טפחים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא קוֹרָה מִשּׁוּם הֶיכֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation from step 2. Both sides now agree the קורה is a היכר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the underlying reason for the dispute over one טפח versus four טפחים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether a ground-level marker is treated like an overhead marker.

steps.title: Third explanation: a decree in case the raised floor wears down
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both agree that a marker below is like a marker above. They argue whether חכמים required four טפחים out of fear that people walking on it will wear the raised area down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: everyone agrees that a marker below is like a marker above. Here they argue about a decree, in case it gets diminished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third possible explanation. On the basic law both sides agree; they only argue about a protective decree (גזירה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly speaking, one טפח of raised floor would be enough. אביי worries that people walking on it will wear it down below one טפח, which would leave the alley unfixed without anyone noticing. So he requires four טפחים as a safety margin. רב יוסף does not worry about this.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective safeguard
Lest it be diminished (worn down)
They disagree (contracted form of קָא מִיפַּלְגִי)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives three explanations for the one-טפח versus four-טפחים dispute: (1) the קורה is a היכר or a מחיצה; (2) whether a marker below equals a marker above; (3) whether there is a גזירה in case the raised floor wears down. Each explanation moves more of the shared ground into agreement and narrows what the two sides actually argue about.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone agrees we say:

phrases.aramaic: הֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַטָּה כְּהֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַעְלָה,
phrases.english: a marker below is like a marker above,
and here they disagree about a decree lest it be diminished.
phrases.notes: אביי makes the decree and requires four טפחים; רב יוסף does not, so one טפח is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אָמְרִינַן הֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַטָּה כְּהֶיכֵּר שֶׁל מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the principle that step 3 left disputed (a marker below equals a marker above) as agreed by everyone, and moves the dispute to a protective decree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If everyone agrees on the basic law, what is left to argue about?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether חכמים decreed four טפחים out of concern that the raised floor will wear down.

steps.title: Digging out the floor under a low beam: how much?
steps.stepSummary: A new case: the קורה is lower than ten טפחים, and he digs out the ground beneath it to reach ten. How much must he dig?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the beam was less than ten handbreadths high, and he dug out the ground under it to complete the height to ten, how much must he dig?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case and asks a question about it. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קורה must be at least ten טפחים above the ground. Instead of raising the beam, this person lowers the floor by digging. The question 'how much must he dig?' is ambiguous, and the next step will point that out.

keyTerms.meaning: Dug out or hollowed out the ground
To complete the height to ten טפחים
Handbreadths, a unit of measurement

phrases.english: If it (the beam) was less than ten handbreadths high
and he dug out under it to complete it to ten,
how much must he dig?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about a קורה that is too low, after the earlier discussion of a raised floor.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much digging is needed when the floor is lowered to bring the קורה up to ten טפחים.

steps.title: The depth question is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the depth is obvious: he digs as much as he needs to reach ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much must he dig?! As much as he needs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own question. The depth is obvious: he digs until the height reaches ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is nothing to ask about the depth, because the target height is already known. The objection forces the question to be reworded so it asks about something that really is unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as he needs

phrases.english: How much must he dig?!
As much as he needs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the question in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question about how deep to dig.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The depth is obviously whatever brings the height to ten, so the question has no content.

steps.title: The real question: how long must the dug area be?
steps.stepSummary: The question is reworded: how far must the dug-out area stretch into the מבוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how far must it extend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rewords its question. It is not asking about depth but about length: how far into the מבוי must the dug-out area reach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dug-out spot under the beam forms a small lowered strip. Only if that strip is long enough does the area count as a proper מבוי entrance with a valid ten-טפחים beam.

keyTerms.meaning: Its length, meaning how far it extends

phrases.english: Rather, how far must it extend?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 6 by fixing what the question means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about the depth of the digging.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about the length of the dug-out area into the מבוי.

steps.title: Four handbreadths or four cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the dug area must extend four טפחים. אביי says four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: four handbreadths. אביי said: four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. רב יוסף requires only four טפחים of length, while אביי requires four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four טפחים is a small but meaningful size in הלכה. Four אמות is the minimum length of a מבוי, so אביי seems to treat the dug-out area as needing the size of a real מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Four טפחים (handbreadths)
Four cubits, a much larger measure

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: four טפחים. אביי: four אמות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two numbers. Four טפחים is about a third of a meter. Four אמות is about two meters, roughly six times longer.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: four handbreadths,
Abaye said: four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר בְּאַרְבָּעָה אַבָּיֵי אָמַר בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף: four טפחים. אביי: four אמות.

steps.title: Is this argument tied to רבי אמי and רבי אסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב יוסף and אביי are really arguing about a ruling of רבי אמי ורבי אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that they disagree about the ruling of רבי אמי and רבי אסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a reason behind the argument. This line sets up the next move, where the earlier ruling is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא often checks whether an argument between later אמוראים depends on an earlier ruling. Here it suggests that the four-טפחים view matches רבי אמי, and the four-אמות view does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion
They disagree

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא בִּדְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about the ruling of Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּדְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to find the root of the argument in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument depends on the ruling of רבי אמי ורבי אסי.

steps.title: The ruling about a breached alley wall
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי ורבי אסי rule about a מבוי whose side wall broke near the entrance. If a פס of four טפחים remains, the beam still works even with a breach up to ten אמות. Without it, a breach of less than three טפחים is fine, but three or more is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: an alley whose side wall was breached near its entrance. It was stated in the name of רבי אמי and רבי אסי: if there is a board of four handbreadths there, it permits even with a breach of up to ten. If not, a breach of less than three permits, but three does not permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ruling it plans to compare. A strip of wall only four טפחים wide is enough to keep the מבוי valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אמי, a short four-טפחים strip still counts as a real piece of wall. Without such a strip, only a gap smaller than three טפחים is allowed, because of לבוד, which treats very small gaps as closed. This four-טפחים idea is what links the ruling to רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: An alley whose wall was broken open
An upright board or strip of wall
A breach or gap
Permits carrying (makes the alley valid)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִיתְּמַר: מָבוֹי שֶׁנִּפְרַץ מִצִּידּוֹ כְּלַפֵּי רֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: As it was stated: an alley that was breached on its side, toward its entrance,

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: it was stated in the name of Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi:
if there is a board of four handbreadths there,
it permits even with a breach of up to ten (cubits).
And if not, less than three (handbreadths) permits.
Three does not permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר מָבוֹי שֶׁנִּפְרַץ מִצִּידּוֹ כְּלַפֵּי רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source mentioned in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a four-טפחים segment is enough to count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי אמי ורבי אסי about a breached מבוי.

steps.title: Matching each view to רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion: רב יוסף follows רבי אמי, and אביי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף holds like רבי אמי. אביי does not hold like רבי אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion by matching each side to the earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's four טפחים fits רבי אמי, who says a four-טפחים strip counts. אביי's four אמות seems to reject that idea, since it would mean four טפחים is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (agrees with) this view
He does not hold this view

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב יוֹסֵף אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef holds like Rabbi Ami,
Abaye does not hold like Rabbi Ami.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַב יוֹסֵף אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling from step 10 to the two views in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The suggestion: רב יוסף agrees with רבי אמי, and אביי disagrees.

steps.title: A damaged alley is different from a new one
steps.stepSummary: אביי could say the cases are different. רבי אמי speaks about a valid מבוי that was later damaged. Here the מבוי is only now being created, so it needs a full four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could say to you: there, it is the end of an alley. Here, it is the beginning of an alley. If there are four cubits, yes. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. אביי can fully agree with רבי אמי, because the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אמי's case, the מבוי was already valid and then broke, so a small four-טפחים strip is enough to keep it going. In our case, the dug-out area is what creates the valid מבוי in the first place. Something being created needs the full minimum size of a מבוי, which is four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you
The end stage of an alley: one already valid that was later damaged
The start of an alley: one being made valid now

steps.whatToRemember: Keeping an existing מבוי valid is easier than creating a new one. So אביי can agree with רבי אמי and still require four אמות here.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that keeping something going is easier than starting it shows up in many places in הלכה. It explains why the same four-טפחים measure can work in one case and fail in another.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'end' and 'beginning' do not mean the two ends of the alley's length. They mean stages in time: after the מבוי was already valid, versus while it is first being set up.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: הָתָם סוֹף מָבוֹי,
phrases.english: Abaye could say to you: there, it is the end stage of an alley,
here, it is the beginning of an alley.
If there are four cubits, yes (it is valid),
if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי הָתָם סוֹף מָבוֹי הָכָא תְּחִלַּת מָבוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link proposed in steps 9 to 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that אביי disagrees with רבי אמי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion treated a damaged existing מבוי the same as a מבוי being created. Creating one requires the full four אמות.

steps.title: אביי brings his source: courtyards must open into the alleyway
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: a מבוי is only permitted with a לחי or קורה if houses and courtyards open into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches that a מבוי can only be made permitted with a לחי or a קורה if houses and courtyards open into it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to back up his view that the area must be four אמות. This sets up his challenge against רב יוסף in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא defines a real מבוי: courtyards must open into it. Every courtyard doorway needs some width. אביי will use this to show that a very short מבוי has no room for these doorways.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an introduction to a proof)
A side post at the entrance of a מבוי
A cross beam over the entrance of a מבוי
Houses and courtyards

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say it?
As it was taught: An alleyway is not permitted
by a side post or a cross beam
unless there are houses and courtyards
opening into it.
phrases.notes: The houses open into the courtyards, and the courtyards open into the alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא (step 12) already showed that אביי can agree with רבי אמי. Now אביי himself brings a positive proof for his own view of four אמות.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that the dug area must be four אמות long
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring houses and courtyards to open into the מבוי

steps.title: A four-handbreadth alleyway has no room for courtyards
steps.stepSummary: If the מבוי is only four טפחים long, how could courtyards open into it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the מבוי is only four טפחים, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף. A מבוי that is only four טפחים long seems too small to have courtyard doorways opening into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needs at least two courtyards, and each doorway is at least four טפחים wide. Two doorways cannot fit along a length of only four טפחים. So רב יוסף's measurement seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find it? (meaning the case seems impossible)
Handbreadths (much smaller than אמות)

phrases.english: And if it is only four handbreadths,
how can you find such a case!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This applies the ברייתא from step 13 against רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that four טפחים is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Courtyard doorways need width. Four טפחים of length cannot hold the doorways the ברייתא requires.

steps.title: Opening through the back wall does not work
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say the courtyards open through the back wall. But רב נחמן says a מבוי must be longer than it is wide, so this answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the courtyards open through the middle wall, didn't רב נחמן say: We have a tradition that a מבוי permitted with a לחי or קורה is one whose length is greater than its width, with houses and courtyards opening into it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible defense for רב יוסף and then knocks it down right away. The challenge against רב יוסף stays standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense: let the back wall be wide enough for two doorways. But then the מבוי is wider than it is long, since it is only four טפחים long. רב נחמן's rule says such a shape is not a valid מבוי, so this defense is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a possible answer that will be rejected)
The middle wall, meaning the back wall facing the entrance
We hold, as a received tradition
Its length is greater than its width

steps.confusionAlert: "Middle wall" does not mean a wall in the middle of the מבוי. It is the back wall, which sits in the middle between the two side walls.

phrases.english: And if you say that it opens
through the middle wall,
phrases.notes: The back wall, which can be made wide enough for two doorways.

phrases.english: but didn't Rav Nachman say: We hold by tradition:
Which alleyway is permitted by a side post or a cross beam?
Any whose length is greater than its width,
and has houses and courtyards opening into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּפָתַח לֵהּ בְּדוֹפֶן הָאֶמְצָעִי, וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This blocks one possible way out of the challenge in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that the courtyards open through the back wall
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the מבוי wider than it is long, against רב נחמן's tradition.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב נחמן's rule that a מבוי must be longer than it is wide is a basic definition of a מבוי.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the doorways open at the corners
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the courtyards open at the corners of the מבוי, so a four-טפחים length is still possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רב יוסף answer? The courtyards open into the מבוי at its corners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge. The courtyard doorways sit at the back corners of the מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A corner doorway uses part of the side wall and part of the back wall. This way each doorway gets its four טפחים without making the מבוי wider than it is long. So the ברייתא and רב נחמן both fit a four-טפחים מבוי, and אביי's proof is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: A corner

steps.whatToRemember: אביי proves four אמות from the ברייתא about courtyards. רב יוסף keeps his four טפחים by placing the courtyard doorways at the corners. This keeps the length greater than the width, as רב נחמן requires.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef?
It is where it opens at the corner.
phrases.notes: Each doorway wraps around a corner, using part of the side wall and part of the back wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף: דְּפָתַח לֵיה בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of steps 14 and 15 on רב יוסף's behalf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-imagining the physical layout of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A four-טפחים מבוי seemed to have no room for courtyard doorways unless it was wider than it was long.
steps.terutzMaskana: Corner doorways give each courtyard enough width while the מבוי stays longer than it is wide.

steps.title: אביי brings proof from a protruding side post
steps.stepSummary: אביי supports his view that a מבוי needs four אמות. He cites רב הונא: a protruding לחי shorter than four אמות counts as a לחי, but at four אמות it counts as a מבוי that needs its own לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know this? Because רמי בר חמא said in the name of רב הונא: a side post that sticks out from the wall of a מבוי, if it is less than four אמות long, is treated as a לחי, and no other לחי is needed to permit carrying. If it is four אמות long, it is treated as a מבוי, and another לחי is needed to permit carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a source to prove his position that a מבוי must be at least four אמות long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule shows that a wall section shorter than four אמות is only a לחי, not a מבוי. Only at four אמות does it turn into a מבוי of its own. So, אביי argues, four אמות is the minimum length of a מבוי, against רב יוסף's four טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an opening for bringing a proof)
A side post at the entrance of a מבוי that permits carrying inside
That sticks out / protrudes
Is treated as / is judged as
Cubits (one אמה is about six טפחים)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up אמות and טפחים. Four אמות is about 24 טפחים, so it is far longer than four טפחים. That size gap is the whole argument between אביי and רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say it?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: For Rami bar Chama said that Rav Huna said:
A side post that sticks out from the wall of an alleyway,
if it is less than four cubits,
it is treated as a side post,
and it does not need another side post to permit it.
If it is four cubits, it is treated as an alleyway,
phrases.notes: The protruding stretch becomes a small alleyway of its own.

phrases.english: and it needs another side post to permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף answered the difficulty from the ברייתא, אביי brings a new proof for his four-אמות position.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that a מבוי needs a length of four אמות
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling (via רמי בר חמא) that a protruding wall under four אמות is a לחי, and at four אמות it is a מבוי

steps.title: רב יוסף separates losing side-post status from becoming an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that four אמות is only needed to strip a protrusion of its לחי status. A new מבוי can exist with just four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would רב יוסף answer? He would say: to remove something from the category of a לחי, you need four אמות. But to count as a מבוי at all, even four טפחים is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב יוסף would respond to אביי's proof, and gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says רב הונא's case is about something that already works as a לחי. Its לחי status does not go away until it reaches four אמות. That says nothing about the minimum size of a new מבוי, which can be just four טפחים, so אביי's proof does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: To take out / to remove
The status or category of a side post
Handbreadths (much smaller than אמות)
Also / too

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's rule: losing לחי status takes four אמות, but becoming a מבוי takes only four טפחים. Two different questions can have two different measurements.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef? (How would he answer?)
To take it out of the status of a side post
requires that there be four cubits.
But to be an alleyway,
even with four handbreadths
it is also an alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof from Step 17 by showing that רב הונא's case is about a different question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself, not רב הונא's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי treated 'no longer a לחי' and 'counts as a מבוי' as the same threshold. רב יוסף says they are two separate thresholds.

steps.title: Studying רמי בר חמא's statement on its own
steps.stepSummary: With the word גופא, the גמרא turns to examine the statement of רמי בר חמא in the name of רב הונא directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רמי בר חמא said in the name of רב הונא: a side post that sticks out from the wall of a מבוי...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It re-quotes the statement it just used as a proof, so that it can now analyze that statement directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב הונא's ruling was only used as a tool in the debate between אביי and רב יוסף. The word גופא tells us the גמרא will now study the ruling for its own sake. The quote continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (a marker that the גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted earlier)
Its side wall

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of the proof. The גמרא repeats the words on purpose to open a fresh discussion of this ruling.

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said that Rav Huna said:
A side post that sticks out from the wall of an alleyway

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אביי and רב יוסף debate and opens a direct analysis of the source quoted in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Re-quotes רב הונא's ruling about a protruding לחי as the base text for a new analysis (the quote continues on the next amud).
